thread:
nora: Heads up — the streaming sample app we ship in the Go repo leaks goroutines if the caller cancels mid-response. Repro steps in the sample: start generator, cancel context after first chunk, observe ~2 goroutines left per stream.

ben: ack, saw that too on my laptop. pretty sure it's the internal ack channel we use for the generator handshake not being closed on ctx.Done().

ashwin: can you paste the minimal repro?

nora: sure. simplified snippet from the sample app: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() {
  time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()
for iter.Next() {
  _ = iter.Token()
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
  fmt.Println("iter err:", err)
}
```
After cancel the iterator stops yielding but a goroutine sticks around in generator.go:handshakeLoop reading from ackCh.

chris: ugh. i thought we already handled that in the handshake refactor. Dev-bot, can you link the issue?

dev-bot: Created issue #371: "go-sdk: generator iterator ackCh not closed on ctx cancel" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/371

ben: quick patch idea: select on ctx.Done() in handshakeLoop and close ackCh from that branch before returning. But need to be careful about double-close races (other path might close it).

ashwin: right — safer pattern is to make ackCh a receive-only channel to the reader and have the writer close it once only. If ctx cancels, signal the writer to stop and let it close. In practice that's a lot of plumbing. Another approach: add a Finalize() on generator.Iterator that callers can call in defer to ensure cleanup.

nora: i'm not thrilled by requiring users to call Finalize(). This is onboarding friction — sample apps should just work out of the box. We should fix the runtime so iterator cleanup is automatic when ctx is canceled.

ben: agreed. propose: when creating the iterator, spawn a goroutine that waits on ctx.Done() and then calls internal.cancelHandshake() which is idempotent. That helper uses sync.Once to close the ack channel exactly once. minimal risk.

chris: sounds OK. also need tests. integration test that cancels after first token and uses runtime/pprof to assert goroutine count returns to baseline within 100ms.

nora: and update the sample app to use a shorter example showing cancellation with a `defer iter.Close()` just in case. Docs note: prefer ctx cancellation, but samples should show both patterns.

ashwin: small API ergonomics thought: our current Generator iterator exposes Next() + Token() + Err() pair. Maybe add a convenience `ForEach(ctx, fn)` helper so users don't have to manage Next/Err for one-off usage. That could reduce leaks from misuse in samples.

ben: +1 on ForEach. though it should accept a context too so it can stop early. Implementation would internally handle handshake cleanup.

chris: can we keep both? low friction ForEach for onboarding, plus manual iterator for advanced usage where people want per-token control.

nora: yep. For docs, add a short note about cancellation patterns and show the ForEach example and the manual with `defer iter.Close()` for advanced. Also link to issue #371.

dev-bot: Milestone updated: patch queued for v0.14.2, PR draft opened by @ben referencing #371.

ben: i'll draft a small PR today with sync.Once approach + unit test for handshake close and an integration test for sample app cleanup.

ashwin: i'll review. also check that the Dedicated runtime uses the same handshake path — we don't want the bug mirrored there.

nora: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. once PR lands i'll update the sample app and the onboarding README to reflect the ForEach convenience.

chris: minor UX ask: can we also make the generator iterator implement io.Closer? that maps to existing Go expectations and makes it easy to `defer iter.Close()` without adding a new method name.

ben: good call. i'll make it implement io.Closer in the PR.

nora: perfect. this should help reduce onboarding friction for teams copy/pasting the sample. :rocket:

chris: sounds like a plan. follow-ups: @ben will open PR, @ashwin will audit Dedicated paths, @nora will update sample app. ping here when ready.
